description.narrative:
Insatsen är en förberedelsefas inför ett tilltänkt större program inom området sysselsättning med anständiga arbetsvillkor. ILO initierade dialog med Sida i augusti 2021 och har sedan dess utarbetat ett konceptpapper som beskriver ett program for inkluderande marknadssystemutveckling i samarbete med UNHCR. Konceptet beskriver en nexusansats till sysselsättning som är relevant både för sysselsättnings- och försörjningsmål i Sida:s förväntade reformstrategi i Östeuropa 2022-28.
Inceptionsprojektet är kopplat till en förenklad beredning med inslag av systemanalys, scenarioanalys av relevanta genomförandealternativ och ett förslag på design av ett långsiktigt expansionsscenario som efter inledande analyser bedöms ha störst resultatpotential i förhållande til sin budget.

The intervention is an inception and design phase in preparation of a larger intended programme in the area of Decent Work. ILO initiated discussions in August 2021, and have since then drafted a concept note for a Market Systems Development programme in the area of Decent Work in partnership with UNHCR. Decent Work aligns with Sida's expected strategy goals for Eastern Europe 2022-28.
The inception phase is carried out as a simplified contribution with elements of market systems analysis, scenario analysis of relevant programming scenarios and a design proposal for the scenario which is perceived to have the best results potential compared with the budget.

The objective of this intervention is to conduct research and design a program for improved employment opportunities for vulnerable people in Ukraine.
The first part of the objective involves assessing vulnerability factors which are of particular relevance i the given context, and collect and analyze primary and secondary data of relevance for the employment situation of the target group.
The second part of the goal is to design a long-term program in line with the results from the research. The program proposal should meet the highest possible requirements for aid effectiveness and is adapted to Sida's overall requirements for development cooperation within the target area.
ILO and UNHCR contribute with complementary institutional experiences to establishing operation in the nexus between humanitarian aid, longt term development needs and conflict sensitivity.
An indirect objective of the intervention relates to how an inclusive market systems assessment and operationalization can improve a joint understanding and capacity for ILO, UNHCR, Sida and local stakeholder with regards to sustainable livelihoods for vulnerable groups in Ukraine. Improved capacity across a range of critical actors is likely to generate effects beyond any particular programme, and enables an advanced dialogue on nexus challenges from Ukraine going forward. (Most notably the integration of short and longer term support in context of war.)

ILO has presented their research studies and a proposal for a roll-out phase of the intervention.
The studies showed that the intervention is much relevant. However, Sida took the decision not to continue with the project due to the changed circumstances brought on by Russia's full-scale war and a different form of project was required.
Sida has continued the dialogue with ILO to design a new project proposal that builds on the results and lessons learned from the inception phase.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
